frontier.hypothesis: Invert the loop's primary induction variable: iterate the loop by the doubled byte-table index j (stepping by 2, matching $fp's own step) and derive the store index i as j >> 1 (matching $s6's exact relationship to $fp, i.e. fp = s6*2 throughout the whole function) -- untried in any prior session; distinct from both killed shared-VALUE spellings because it changes which variable is the loop's PRIMARY biv rather than sharing a derived value.
frontier.mechanism: loop.c strength-reduction on TWO givens with a fixed linear relationship to the same basic induction variable: if the original C's loop variable was genuinely the doubled index (not i), GCC's normal single-induction-variable codegen for THAT variable would naturally produce $fp's exact pattern (one multiply at loop entry, +=2 per iteration), while i = j>>1 (or an inline shift at the store site) would separately explain $s6's +=1 pattern if loop.c recognizes j>>1 as a second, independently-reducible given of the same loop.
frontier.next_probe: Rewrite the loop as for (j = start*2; j < start*2+4; j += 2) with i = j >> 1 computed once per iteration (or the store address computed inline via arg0 + 0x444 + (j>>1)), sandbox it on the s7-banked chassis. If neutral-or-better, this is the real structural fix (continue narrowing); if worse, it kills the 'original loop was indexed by the doubled value' hypothesis outright and $fp must be attributed to a delay-slot/scheduling artifact independent of loop shape -- worth an immediate solver-modality inverse_compose.py re-classify either way, since this is the first C change since s8's classify run with any chance of moving the verdict off PRE-RA.
